svg.text: TEAM ZIG · BLUE REWARDS · SYSTEMS MAP
An enhanced experience within Blue Rewards
+ same direction · − opposite direction · ‖ significant delay · R reinforcing, B balancing
Available value does not reliably become realized value.
Members miss opportunities worth having, cannot tell what they are owed, and give up when value goes missing. Realized value is the main variable.
should raise realized value — but its return leg is unconfirmed
caps realized value by limiting how generous offers can be
drains realized value by turning delay into withdrawal
One minus and a delay. The lag before a member can confirm that a purchase
counted, or that a missing reward is being handled, is what manufactures doubt.
privacy law, consent rules, suitability, disclosure
PC Optimum, Scene, bank and card ecosystems
formed by every other app they use, and not always realistic
a member, a BMO client, or both
what the enhancement is built around
What the programme records is what
a member did inside it, not everything
Owns Blue Rewards and funds it. Emerging Business, in gold, is our client.
Each of the other teams holds a decision we would need.
carries the cost of points held
The loyalty programme itself: the offers, the points, the catalogue, and the people who resolve cases.
We would read from these services and write back to them. We would not replace any of them.
WHAT WE ARE PROPOSING TO BUILD
An enhanced experience within the Blue Rewards app and website
ranked options, with the reason for the ranking
a saved goal and a saved comparison
what has arrived, and what is still expected
a case the member can follow
the same saved information, in their own words
No single party sees a whole journey, so when value goes missing the evidence is
split between them. Each sends what it has on its own schedule, so the programme
often finds out late. We would ask all five and instruct none.
writes the eligibility rules, the reward amount and the deadlines
the only party that sees what was actually in the basket
sees a merchant and an amount, and decides when it settles
ties an online click or a photographed receipt to the member
ships the gift card, books the trip, decides when it arrives
‖ delay — they report on their own timeline
+ we send each case to them
Who this reaches, and what it would mean for them
Fewer steps and less uncertainty, and a way to see what is owed
Recovered points reduce breakage, and liability ages differently
Inquiries rise before they fall, because loss becomes visible
Ranking changes who gets seen, and who does not
More reason to hold the card, but only if the flywheel turns
Each one changes a loop above. Grouped under the three candidate leverage points in the faculty brief.
Not issued value, not activity, not breakage. Changes what the scoreboard rewards, so it changes B1.
Make what is earned, pending, posted and used visible as one thing. Shortens the delay in B2.
Find at-risk value early and route it. This is the recovery capability.
Intrusion spends it, so personalization has a ceiling. Caps how hard R1 can be pushed.
Feed what actually arrived back into relevance. This is the return leg of R1.
• Existing earning methods: partner scans, linked-card offers, receipts, Shops and BMO products.
• Redemption fulfilment: gift cards, travel, merchandise and partner redemptions.
• BMO and partner support where manual investigation or partner action is required.
• Partner issuance, redemption and reversal: those services need partner credentials, not a member session.
